title: Vectors in CockroachDB
chunk: CockroachDB stores embeddings in a VECTOR column alongside relational data, so the vector and the record it describes are written in the same transaction. There is no separate vector store to keep in sync.

title: Vector Indexing
chunk: A vector index in CockroachDB uses approximate nearest-neighbor search over partitions built with k-means clustering. It is generally available in v26.2 and enabled with the feature.vector_index.enabled cluster setting.

title: The CockroachDB Operator
chunk: On Kubernetes, CockroachDB is deployed by the GA CockroachDB Operator using CrdbCluster and CrdbNode custom resources. There are no StatefulSets; the operator can replace any node freely and reuse its disk.

title: Resilience and Consensus
chunk: CockroachDB replicates every range across nodes and commits writes by majority consensus using Raft. Losing a single node costs no committed data because a majority of replicas still hold it.

title: Stateless RAG App
chunk: The RAG application is a stateless FastAPI service. All durable state lives in CockroachDB, which lets Kubernetes scale, kill, and reschedule the app pods freely without data loss.

title: Autoscaling on Custom Metrics
chunk: A RAG request is often latency-bound waiting on an LLM, so CPU can look idle under load. The Horizontal Pod Autoscaler should scale on a custom metric such as requests per second per pod to reflect real demand.

title: Liveness vs Readiness
chunk: A liveness probe asks whether the process is alive; failing it restarts the container. A readiness probe asks whether the pod can serve traffic; failing it removes the pod from the Service without restarting it. A lost database should make the app not ready, not dead.

title: Transaction Retries
chunk: Because CockroachDB offers serializable isolation, under contention it may return a retry error (40001). This is expected; application code should wrap transactions in a retry loop rather than surfacing these as failures.
